display.title: Episode 527: King David's Grave
display.summary_short: A Sefirah-time show: listeners' letters, Pirkei Avos chapter 2 on the eye that sees and the ear that hears, Shema with two brothers, and the story of the king's sword lost in King David's tomb.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens straight into his mailbox: a girl's original poem about the Pesach Seder and a boy's letter about dressing up as Mordechai for Purim. In the days of Sefirah, between Pesach and Shavuos, we work on our character and learn Pirkei Avos. This week's chapter teaches how to stay humble and do only what is right: remember the eye that sees, the ear that hears, and the book in which all our deeds are written before Hashem. Two brothers recite the Shema in Studio 604, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time honors Dovid HaMelech, whose yahrzeit is on Shavuos. A visiting king drops his precious royal sword into the sealed cave of King David's tomb in Yerushalayim. His servants who go down never come back, but after the Jewish community says the whole Tehillim, the town's rabbi is lowered in and returns with the sword, having seen only a bright light. The king grants the Jews freedom to keep the Torah. The show ends with a call to learn the Twelve Pesukim and to say Tehillim chapter 20 for the Rebbe's recovery.
display.lesson: Remember that Hashem sees, hears and records everything we do, and trust Him to protect us; Dovid HaMelech is truly alive.
